title: How to organise the china or display cabinet | Dining Room
description:
Keep the good tableware safe, visible, and genuinely usable.

This is the China or Display Cabinet in the Dining Room. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Plates stacked no more than eight high with felt between them, cups standing single file rather than nested, glasses rim up on a clean liner, tureens on the bottom shelf, the cabinet strapped to a wall stud, and a photo of the finished shelves taped inside the door.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Take every piece out and split it into three groups: complete sets, chipped or crazed pieces, and lone survivo
Straighten: Tureens and heavy serving pieces on the bottom shelf, plates and bowls at hand height, ceremonial pieces up to
Shine: Wash by hand in a plastic basin with a towel in the bottom, never the dishwasher for gilt rims or hand paintin
Safety: Strap the cabinet to a wall stud, because a tall glass-fronted case loaded with plates is the heaviest tip-ove
Standardize: Photograph the finished shelves and tape the picture inside the door so the china goes back the same way after
Sustain: After any meal that used the good china, it is hand-washed, dried, and back behind the glass before anyone tur

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
A shelf photo inside the door, eight plates at most per stack with felt between, the weight on the bottom shelf, and the cabinet strapped to the wall.
